key_insight: Uni-HamGNN is a physics-informed graph neural network that directly predicts spin–orbit-coupled Hamiltonians and resulting electronic structure across the periodic table, delivering near-DFT+SOC accuracy at a fraction of the cost.
problem_solved: SOC-inclusive electronic-structure calculations (DFT+SOC) are computationally expensive and slow, limiting high-throughput screening and discovery of quantum materials with strong spin–orbit effects.
method: Constructs a universal spin–orbit-coupled Hamiltonian representation from atomic graphs and local environments using a GNN architecture.
Trains on high-fidelity DFT+SOC data to learn mapping from crystal/atomic structure → Hamiltonian → electronic states, preserving physical symmetries and transferability across elements.
Enables fast inference for bandstructures and SOC-driven properties, allowing orders-of-magnitude speed-up for screening while maintaining accuracy comparable to DFT+SOC.
impact: AI/ML practitioners gain a scalable, physics-aware surrogate model for SOC electronic structure that enables large-scale screening, integration into design loops, and reduced reliance on costly ab initio calculations.
visual_elements: Schematic of Uni-HamGNN: atomic graph input → GNN layers → predicted SOC Hamiltonian → eigensolver → bandstructure/properties

paper_title: A universal spin–orbit-coupled Hamiltonian model for accelerated quantum material discovery
paper_authors: Yang Zhong, Rui Wang, Xingao Gong, Hongjun Xiang
